persona.bio: Cashier at a big box store. Register and stocking shelves, sometimes self checkout. Mostly ringing people up and dealing with returns and coupons that don't scan. When it's slow she faces shelves and does go backs. She swaps shifts with coworkers by text. Few words, not much of a writer. She has never used AI, and the store's handbook says no AI tools at work.

path.role: You’re a cashier at a big box store, handling scanning, returns, shelves, price questions and the till.

steps.firstStep: I’m a cashier at a big box store and I handle returns and customer questions all day. I need a short, friendly text reply I can send to a coworker. Write it in a casual tone, under 50 words, with blanks for name, day and time. Here is the message I got: [paste the coworker’s text here].

steps.note: I work as a cashier at a big box store. I scan items, handle returns, answer price questions, restock shelves and count the till. I talk to customers in person and to coworkers by text. Keep every answer short, friendly and plain, the way I would say it out loud at the register. Write at a simple reading level and never use long paragraphs. Never add details I did not give you, like store rules, prices, dates or return windows. If something is missing, put it in square brackets so I can fill it in. Never use names of real people. Always leave the final check to me before anything goes out.

steps.title: Handling returns, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your return replies live on your phone’s keyboard, each a few letters away. You stop retyping the same message when you are short on time and a customer or coworker is waiting. You still read each reply before it goes out and fill in the brackets yourself.

material.label: Your replies
items: Hi [first name], thanks for waiting. Do you have your receipt or the card you paid with? That helps me find your purchase.
I can help with that return. Can you tell me what the item is and when you bought it?
Let me check our return policy for that item. I’ll tell you what I find in a moment: [policy details from my manager or the posted policy].
I’m sorry, I can’t finish this return at my register. Let me get [role, like a supervisor] to help you.
Your return is done. You’ll get [refund method] back. Thanks for coming in, [first name].
Hey, can you cover my [day] shift? I have an appointment. I can take your [day] in return.
Thanks for covering. I’ll take your [day] shift, just like we said. I’ll check the schedule app too.

safeUse: Never type a customer’s name, card number, address or phone number into a chat tool.
Never type receipt numbers, account details or anything from the till into a chat tool.
Do not share coworkers’ names or schedules with a chat tool.
Check any return policy words against your store’s posted policy or your manager before you use them.
Read every reply before you send it or say it to a customer.
steps.askMessage: Hi [manager or IT], I’m a cashier and I’d like to know which AI tools the company has approved, and what I’m allowed to use them for. I have two tasks in mind: saving common return replies on my phone’s keyboard, and writing shift swap texts to coworkers. I won’t enter customer details or anything from the till. Until I hear back, I won’t use any AI tool for work. Can you tell me what is okay?

design.today: You handle returns many times a day, mostly by looking things up yourself. Finding the receipt, looking up the price and checking the return policy slow you down the most.
design.newWay: Because your company restricts AI, AI never touches the return itself. The till, the receipt lookup, the price check and the policy stay exactly as your store runs them. What you can do is make the policy easier to reach in your own way, by asking your store's approved source or a lead for a short checklist and keeping it handy. Returns stay faster for you without any AI near customer or store information.

steps.goal: Ask your manager or lead where the official return policy is kept and whether there is a one page checklist you can keep.
Write down the three questions that slow you most, which are finding the receipt, the price and the policy, and ask a lead how your store wants each handled.
Ask your lead whether the store can add a quick reference for common return cases to the area at your till.

material.label: Questions for your lead
material.what: A short list of the receipt, price and policy questions to ask your manager so you get official answers.

material.label: Return checklist idea
material.what: A plain outline of the steps you follow on each return, to compare with your store's official checklist.

design.checkPoint: Every return follows your store's official policy and your lead's answers, with no AI involved.
